key_insight: UniGenDet unifies generative and discriminative models in a co-evolutionary training loop so generators improve realism while detectors become more robust to new synthetic artifacts, yielding mutually beneficial gains for both tasks.
problem_solved: Bridges the disconnect between standalone image generators and detectors—addressing the arms-race where generators evade detectors and detectors overfit to specific synthesis methods—by enabling joint, adversarially informed learning.
method: Introduce a unified framework that trains a generator and a detector together in a co-evolutionary loop so each model continually challenges and improves the other.

Exchange adversarial signals and shared feature representations between networks (e.g., discriminative feedback to guide generator artifacts mitigation and generator-driven hard negatives to strengthen the detector).
Optimize a combined objective balancing image realism and detection sensitivity, with curriculum or adaptive weighting to stabilize training and prevent collapse.
impact: Enables more realistic synthetic image generation while producing detectors that generalize better to novel generators—useful for safer generative models, more reliable forensics, and practitioners building robust detection pipelines.

paper_title: UniGenDet: A Unified Generative-Discriminative Framework for Co-Evolutionary Image Generation and Generated Image Detection
paper_authors: Yanran Zhang, Wenzhao Zheng, Yifei Li, Bingyao Yu, Yu Zheng
